directAnswer: To set up a subnet mask, access your network settings and specify the desired subnet mask according to your network design.
summary: Configuring a subnet mask is essential for defining network boundaries and facilitating communication between devices.

sections.heading: Understanding Subnet Masks
sections.body: A subnet mask determines which portion of an IP address refers to the network and which part refers to the host. Common subnet masks include 255.255.255.0 for small networks.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: Instructions may vary based on the operating system or router interface.

steps.title: Windows
steps.detail: Go to Control Panel > Network and Internet > Network Connections. Right-click your network adapter, select Properties, then select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and click Properties. Enter the subnet mask in the appropriate field.

steps.title: macOS
steps.detail: Open System Preferences > Network. Select your network interface, click Advanced, then go to the TCP/IP tab. Enter the subnet mask in the Subnet Mask field.

steps.title: Router Configuration
steps.detail: Log in to your router's web interface. Navigate to the LAN settings section, and enter the desired subnet mask in the appropriate field.

faqs.question: What is the default subnet mask for a Class C network?
faqs.answer: The default subnet mask for a Class C network is 255.255.255.0.

faqs.question: Can I use a custom subnet mask?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use a custom subnet mask to create subnets within your network as needed.

faqs.question: What happens if I set the wrong subnet mask?
faqs.answer: Setting the wrong subnet mask can lead to connectivity issues, preventing devices from communicating properly within the network.

caveats: Ensure that the subnet mask matches the IP addressing scheme of your network to avoid conflicts.
